newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt Bank to buy PBI, Prosper -source.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt Bank to buy PBI, Prosper -source.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank has won a tender to buy the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and the ailing Prosper Bank, outbidding Austria's Creditanstalt and U.S. GE Capital, a banking source said.
PBI, which has capital of 197.1 million zlotys, a balance sheet total of 4.56 billion zlotys and which recorded a 55.2 million zloty net profit in 1996, is 100 percent owned by the central bank.
Prosper Bank, 93 percent-owned by the central bank, has capital of 16.1 million zlotys and an accumulated loss of 161 million zlotys. It has a balance sheet total of 557 million zlotys.
Under the conditions of the tender investors who wanted to buy PBI had to buy also Prosper Bank.
At the end of 1996 Kredyt Bank had capital of 219 million zlotys and a net profit of 23.2 million zlotys. Its balance sheet total is 1.07 billion zlotys.
The National Bank of Poland has so far declined comment on the tender and called a news conference on the sale of both banks for Friday afternoon.
